title: Practice 4: Нет, не было: having none

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: This job has no future.
exercises.why: Another use of the genitive is in the phrase "I have...". Though Russian does have the verb 'to have' (**иметь**), it is rarely used. Instead, Russians use the following construction to say "I have X": **У меня есть Х**. This literally means, 'By me exists X'. Since the preposition **у** calls the genitive case, the person or thing that has the object in question is placed in the genitive. The thing that is possessed remains in the nominative: **У** + *gen* + **есть** + *nom* To turn this into a question, place an inflection on **есть**, just as you place an inflection on the verb in a normal question. Conversely, to say 'There isn't...', 'There aren't...', we use the word **нет** followed… — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 27.  ·  «The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative.» «Conversely, to say 'There isn't...', 'There aren't...', we use the word нет followed by the genitive case.» — DLI, Lesson 27; Wikibooks, «Genitive case».
exercises.context: Another use of the genitive is in the phrase "I have...". (From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 27)
